clue.text: One daughter in French region making fortune

indicators.note: the two short pieces sit inside the region's name, as the clue says they are in it

parts.note: Provence is the region of south-east France
one is the Roman numeral I
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl with a share in a French estate comes into money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is the link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is fate or the guiding hand of destiny, which is one sense of fortune.

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
to lift something is to raise it

explanation.surface: An instruction to praise a powerful elevator, or a power lift in weight training.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend someone is to speak well of them, a direct synonym.

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencil leads
something overdue is late

explanation.surface: A library notice about an old fine on an overdue book.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means lately or in the recent past, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Expecting relatives underfoot to go outside

indicators.note: the phrase for being underfoot must go around the word for relatives

parts.note: someone underfoot is in the way
your relatives are your family

explanation.surface: Visiting relations get under your feet and should be sent outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-word phrase meaning underfoot is split after its second word to take in the relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom is an old euphemism for being pregnant, just as expecting is.

clue.text: Seasonal gift of great geese almost cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are messed about with, as when accounts are cooked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the birds is dropped

explanation.surface: A festive table where some great geese are not quite done roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GEESE to GEES; with GREAT that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate egg is the classic present given at the spring holiday, so it is a seasonal gift.

explanation.surface: A teacher praises a lesson delivered with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a teaching session, and quality or elegance of manner.

indicators.note: returning tells us the word for plans comes back the other way

parts.note: maps are plans of an area

explanation.surface: Someone sends their plans back in favour of tinned luncheon meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the well-known brand of tinned pork luncheon meat.

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a claim is an application for something, such as benefits

explanation.surface: Someone states their support for a submitted application.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, a synonym of declare.

indicators.note: unwisely suggests a foolish jumble of these letters

explanation.surface: A landlady foolishly admits a wandering singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval travelling singer and poet, which is what a troubadour was.

parts.note: separate things are distinct or different
tables are charts of data

explanation.surface: A drama showing contrasting diagrams.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a play by Terence Rattigan set in a seaside hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattigan's 1954 pair of one-act dramas carries this title, so it is a specific play.

clue.text: Assign vote, bishop not being present

indicators.note: the bishop is absent, so his letter leaves the word for vote

parts.note: a ballot is a vote
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church election where seats are given out with the bishop away.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or allocate, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: after places the word for unhappy behind the word for climb

parts.note: to scale is to climb
feeling down is feeling unhappy

explanation.surface: A climber, miserable after the ascent, decides to reduce effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce in size or extent is a straight synonym of cutting back.

clue.text: Defiant words, likewise, at that place

parts.note: so means likewise, as in 'so do I'
there means at that place

explanation.surface: A retort said in the same spirit, right on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a triumphant, defiant retort, so it counts as defiant words.

clue.text: Start shielding learner driver beginning to turn red

indicators.note: the fright word wraps around and protects the learner's letter

parts.note: a start is a sudden fright, a scare
L is the learner plate on a novice's car

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A beginner driver is startled at the first turn and goes red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like an instruction to take a first letter; here it is a noun meaning a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of red, so this is an example of the colour.

clue.text: Deceive misbehaving kid at rear of queue, ultimately

indicators.note: a misbehaving child puts the letters into disorder
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A naughty child at the back of a line plays tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to swindle or trick someone, so it is a synonym phrase for deceive.

clue.text: Respect at one time shown round base, current base

indicators.note: the word for at one time is shown wrapped around the rest

parts.note: once means at one time, as in 'once upon a time'
a bed is a base or foundation, as a flower bed or river bed
I is the symbol for electric current
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A tribute to past deference shown around a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: The two uses of 'base' are different: a foundation, then the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is deference or compliance, close to respect in the sense of heeding authority.

clue.text: Renegade given a job at end of debate

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: the end of the word debate is its final letter

explanation.surface: A defector is rewarded with a position once the debate is over.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons their faith or party, which is what a renegade does.

indicators.note: the written work goes about, or around, the border word

parts.note: prose is ordinary written work, as opposed to verse
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: An essay about a flower border in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: One may get fed by the side of the road

definitions.text: One may get fed by the side of the road

parts.words: One may get fed by the side of the road
parts.note: seems to describe a roadside animal or a picnicker, but what gets fed is a coin slot at a kerbside bay

explanation.surface: A stray creature given food at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'feeding' is putting coins into a machine to pay for a parking bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers feed coins into this kerbside machine to pay for time parked beside the road.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A snooze after lunch in the comfiest chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is the traditional Spanish rest taken in the early afternoon.

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a flex is an electric cable or cord

explanation.surface: A memo concerning an electrical lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flex' is the British word for an appliance's power lead, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to write it down or log it, a synonym of the verb.

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet warns that a dose of medicine might disagree with a husky-type dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a fluffy white breed originating with the Samoyedic peoples of Siberia.

clue.text: Lower oneself: dine out entertaining leader of gangsters

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest inside, so the jumbled letters go around
out signals the letters of dine are put out of order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A snob reluctantly eats out with a mob boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns DINE into DEIN, which takes in the G.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend to do something, which is lowering oneself.

clue.text: Picture of 'wise men' feeding in East

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the wise men are fed into the little word

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A painting of the Magi eating in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to imagine it, a verb synonym.

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A passionate declaration of love made by an eager speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship, a synonym of love as a noun.

clue.text: Rope in young woman, obliging initially

parts.note: a lass is a young woman

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word obliging

explanation.surface: A helpful girl is persuaded to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rope in' reads as one phrase, but only 'Rope' is the definition; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a looped rope, so rope as a verb fits.

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of its final letter

parts.note: an event is a competition, as at a sports meeting

explanation.surface: A contest that is almost a draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even is flat or level, and scores that are even are level too.

parts.note: under means beneath
a stand is a raised platform

explanation.surface: An instruction to excavate below a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' is slang for grasp or appreciate, as in 'I dig it', not excavating.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'dig' means to get or comprehend something, the same as grasping it.
